SMTO-PRL-0005 — That conflict choice is out of date

GUID: f9d76e70-8b1c-42d4-a495-bbc07d5257d1
Slug: parallel-rejected-batch-missing
Domain: PRL · Subsystem: prl

What happened

  • You chose how to handle a conflict between steps, but that conflict had already changed or been resolved. Your choice wasn't applied.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the page and reopen the conversation. The conflict you answered may have been replaced or already handled.
  2. If an Action Rejected · Parallel conflict card still appears, open its menu and choose Serialize safely and continue to run the clashing steps one after another. Only the conflict shown now can be settled, and leaving it on Keep rejecting keeps those steps blocked.
  3. If no conflict card appears, let the task continue, or send a message telling SMTO how you'd like it to go on. The earlier conflict no longer blocks the task.

What success looks like

  • The conflict card is gone and the task continues.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to rerun the old blocked steps from memory; let it work from the task as it is now.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A run-scope parallel-execution update named a batch_id that is absent, differs from the run's current foreground batch, or is no longer in the blocked_conflict state.

What this means

  • A policy update names a batch_id that is absent, different from the retained batch, or no longer blocked_conflict. Activity ownership, preflight and durable receipts determine admission and effect certainty. Rejected new work does not erase prior child effects; recovery and diagnostics never replay an unknown operation.

Why this can happen

  • A policy update names a batch_id that is absent, different from the retained batch, or no longer blocked_conflict.

How to diagnose it

  • Refresh the current retained batch and its state without reconstructing old operations.

How to fix it

  • Refresh the run and act on the current foreground_batch; send a policy update with its batch_id only while it is still blocked_conflict. Do not reconstruct or replay the stale rejected batch.
  • Refresh current run controls and address the current decision; do not reconstruct or replay a stale rejected batch.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Any policy decision refers to the current exact blocked batch.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Activity ownership, preflight and durable receipts determine admission and effect certainty. Rejected new work does not erase prior child effects; recovery and diagnostics never replay an unknown operation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
